3D Print Tools

Free browser-based tools for scaling, referencing, and calculating costs for STL conversions for tabletop miniatures. Whether you are printing Warhammer proxies, D&D monsters, or Bolt Action infantry, these tools help you avoid wasted filament. All tools run client-side — no uploads, no accounts, no cookies.

Featured tool

STL Scale Converter

The main STL scale calculator I use before every print. Select source and target scales, choose eye-level or top-of-head, and get the exact slicer percentage for Warhammer, D&D, Bolt Action, Star Wars Legion, and more.

Use the tool
16+ gaming scales Eye Level & Top of Head FDM-optimized percentages No upload, no login

Calculators

Slicer Percentage Calculator

Type in two measurements in millimetres, get the exact percentage for your slicer. Works for any scale combination.

  • Any source size to any target size
  • Real-time calculation as you type
  • 12 common conversion presets
  • Formula breakdown for verification
  • Copy result to clipboard
  • Zero bloat — no account, no cookies

Filament Cost Calculator

Know your print cost before you start. Enter filament price, weight used, and optional electricity to estimate the true cost of 3D printing miniatures.

  • Real-time cost calculation
  • Filament cost per print
  • Optional electricity cost estimate
  • Filament presets with real market prices
  • Deep-link from scale engine
  • No account, no cookies

Real-World Scale Converter

How tall is a 12-foot wall in 32mm scale? Enter any real-world height in feet, inches, or centimetres and get the exact miniature size in millimetres.

  • Feet, inches, or centimetres input

  • Runs entirely in your browser

All tools included

Built for miniature 3D printing

Every tool on STLACCESS is built around one problem I kept running into: getting the right scale for 3D printed tabletop miniatures. The calculator and reference library work together so you can convert and share scale percentages — all from your browser, all for free.

  • STL Scale Engine — The main calculator for converting between any supported scales
  • Scale Reference Library — 46 verified conversion percentages with print-tested results

I build these tools like this

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

All of these tools run entirely in your browser — no backend, no database, no cookies. I built the scale calculator around a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm, the same reference point most of the tabletop miniatures community uses. And I don't publish a conversion percentage until I've printed it myself and measured it with my digital calipers.

I add new scales when wargaming manufacturers release a new system, or when enough of you catch a wrong number through the feedback form. Every percentage is tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini before publishing — if a test print comes off the build plate looking out of proportion with my own army, I tweak the numbers first. I built these tools for my own workflow and put them online so other tabletop printers can save time and filament.
